item.title: Your friendly neighborhood demon: Your friendly neighborhood demon
item.content:encoded:
A completely incompetent demon is summoned by a researcher. The researcher gets terminated and the demon tries (miserably) to do its job.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Mostly comedy, secondly psychological.

Page Layout (Optional):

+ show block
– hide block

Class and ConProcs before and after the “incident”. Description of the Book and, adding the “as of dd/mm/yyyy” the description of the Entity. At least three Interview logs with the entity (or just one log with multiple “extracts” to give the idea). An example of a contract the entity would propose (with a lot of Latin and high-sounding words of jurisprudence to give it an overly serious characterization to contrast the demon’s one) and, finally, a note from Hell itself.

Elevator Pitch:

+ show block
– hide block

SCP will be composed of two parts:
• A book, which the Foundation seized, that describes various thaumaturgical/satanical rituals. One of these being the summoning of demons.
• A weak and lower demon, summoned by a Researcher trying to bargain for money, power, etc. The demon is rather “stupid”. It’s forcibly stuck in the room he was summoned in due to the blood glyph drawn on the floor and his only goal is to acquire as many souls as he can.

Central Narrative:

+ show block
– hide block

The demon acts all high and mighty, like a stereotypical devil from fantasy literature, talking big and trying to sway people into making contracts with him. It is, however, extremely weak and incompetent. Gets easily irritated, lies terribly, and doesn’t seem to be able to trick anyone into doing anything evil. Quite on the contrary it seems that people behave better around him, much to its irritation.
Meanwhile through the interview logs the reader experiences the reaction to the loss of the researcher that summoned it, that was terminated for his abuse. The conversations with the demon will parallel a possible set of reactions to the Foundation methods in dealing with rule breakers.
In the end a note will be found in the site director’s office thanking the Foundation for containing the demon without exorcising him back, humorously hinting that the demon was so incompetent that he was disliked in Hell.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

+ show block
– hide block

Most of the article features a comedic style derived from the stereotypical “big demon” behavior being attributed to such a wimpy and incapable creature, its inefficient methods and, lastly his frustration about it.
On the other, side readers will delve into some possible reactions to the idea that someone you worked with every day, maybe even dated or considered a friend, has been literally killed for breaking the rules at work. Even if working at the Foundation they are still human beings after all.

Additional Notes:

+ show block
– hide block

Hiding behind a copious humorous screen there will be a cynical reasoning about the Foundation methods and, above all, their impact on personnel. I think this "laugh and think" style could prove functional.

item.title: I Have a Idea!: I Have a Idea!
item.content:encoded:
Hi! I'm a new member! And I have two ideas of anomalies, but I wanted to know if there is something similar on the site, or if it was very bizarre both.

My first concept is a manifestation of a humanoid entity in the middle of a lake, she would wear a suit, and along with it would manifest a table with a cup of tea and some documents, the documents would have various ideas of machines that would help the Foundation, and the entity would also use a doctor's plague mask, just a mask, but I think the mask would start saying it was a copy of 049.

My second concept, is an extremely gigantic quadruped entity that can only be seen by certain individuals, made up of buildings, houses, hotels, hotels and these things, the 4 legs would also be composed like this, and all the individuals close to him would be in extreme terror , in more serious cases even killing oneself, within the entity it would be a maze that each room is a bathroom that is the same as the individual's house, or one that he has already seen.

item.title: [Seeking Greenlight] Host of the Eldritch Abomination.: Re: [Seeking Greenlight] Host of the Eldritch Abomination.
item.content:encoded:
Heyo followup! :)

SAND

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

Elevator Pitch: Janual Grey is a mixed-race of a human and a Lovecraftian-horror, he is a space-time, reality-altering Lovecraftian horror who uncontrollably goes on a frenzy to satisfy his hunger when not consuming any nutritious food.

This is much more concise than the initial EP. My only real concern here is the vagueness of the effects; "space-time altering" and "reality altering" are fairly broad terms. What specifically can the skip do?

For this to work, you will need a strong narrative behind it, as the concept on its own won't be enough to carry the article, the frequency this sort of premise is seen, also contributes heavily to this needing a strong narrative. -The concept could appear cliched or hard to get invested in otherwise.

I would recommend you work on exploring the skip itself more in the narrative, and work on expanding on the current points you have in the EP. Other than that however, I don't much of a problem with this initially.

He discovers his powers shortly after the seal implanted by his father has worn off while he's camping at Acadia-National-Park. Due to having a monstrous-form and nature, he didn't want to hurt the innocents, so he ran away from society. During his times in the woods, Janual started to use his powers to transport bad peoples, usually from high-security prisons or those who have faced death penalties, to the forest and consumes them to restrain the hostile nature he embodies.

IMO this doesn't seem necessary to the pitch, as this is fairly specific info that looks closer to what you would see (at least in part) in the narrative summary. That said though, one of my biggest issues is the cannibalism. Considering the skip is compassionate, I have trouble believing that it could justify eating any humans. I'm also unsure on how the skip knows exactly which prisoners are in what sentence. Overall, eating humans (from what I've gathered) is optional for the skip, considering if it really needed to, it could eat an animal or live off wild grown food.

If you want to depict the skip eating other humans; you would need to have a strong reason behind it, along with showing how the skip reacts to/ feels about doing it. If they have morals then doing such a thing would affect them heavily.- as quick note with this, do make sure to handle the topic carefully. Try not to just allow the skip to go and eat people point blank.

The narrative:

Since being held in Foundation custody after reports of prisoners went missing and their corpses being found in the woods. At the same time, they also learned that he has a relationship with SCP-105 as being her school friend and his hungry nature that happened every 24 hours after an incident where he forgot to eat.

I would still recommend you phase SCP-105 out, it doesn't really contribute anything and considering its a series one skip, may be seen as a quick way to gain attention.

The shocking truth was:

His father is an eldritch abomination named "Darkness" worshiped by a cult named "Allies-of-"Darkness" as they have succeeded in summoning it into their reality. Janual's father disguised as a human and seduced his mother into having a baby while visiting the church. When Janual was born, his father secretly implanted a seal to prevent him from exposing his powers. It wants Janual to become the next "Darkness". Janual explained this after the cult was given an order by his father to free him after they've received its "universal-message" through telepathic communications, which also bestowing them reality-bending powers. However, they were killed shortly after finishing the explanation when not paying attention to the MTF arriving.

Overall, this is still closer to an explanation than anything. I'm still not given a clear story arc, or any major events, or any clear idea on how the concept and narrative will be executed in the draft. While there is a story here, it's too vague to really grasp or understand, as there is not lead up or explanation as to how the Foundation knows about certain things (ie. the cult).

My previous concerns with the narrative still hold up. I would highly recommend you start developing a narrative straight away, the context you currently have in place of the narrative can be replaced or taken out if they don't contribute to the overall arc.

Red or green?
Due to my afore mentioned concerns, no-greenlight.

-this needs a narrative more than anything, without one, I wouldn't be comfortable giving a greenlight.

If you would like me review this (or any concept) further, then please feel free to send me a PM or ask via IRC. Response times generally range from 2-12 hours over PMs. If your looking for additional critiques in general, then I would highly recommend contacting the butterfly squad :)

Cheers,

-RED

item.title: Mommy Theres a Man Outside (Seeking Green Lights): Mommy Theres a Man Outside (Seeking Green Lights)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale

Pitch:
SCP-4666 is a terrifying entity force, and essentially unstoppable. The entry log is scary, but how horrifying would it be to be a part of one of the entities hunts?

Central Narrative: The story follows a little boy and his family who live in rural Germany, the story starting off at night with the little boy shouting for his mother "Mommy, mommy! There's a man outside!" the family then doesn't see the man and the story would progress through the different stages of the hunt all the way until the end in which 4666 kills the family and kidnaps the boy the end of the story would then switch perspectives to a boy in rural Ireland who is shouting, "Mommy, mommy! There's a man outside!"

Attention Grabber: Christmas isn't the time for laughter and cheer anymore

Additional Notes: I actually told a story similar to this as a camp fire story, thought it would be interesting as a tale, feedback of any kind is appreciated :) Hope you enjoyed, and hope you're having a Merry Christmas

item.title: A new SCP I'm working on: Re: A new SCP I'm working on
item.content:encoded:
My new idea is that they're using him to test antidotes for poisons and diseases.

I don't know how to have a narrative in an SCP file. I'd compare it to describing a character's personality. You don't tell his entire story, only the bits that have shaped him in major ways.

As for the last question, it's the same as the second one. I'd know how to make him loveable if I was writing a story and I could show his personality through action and dialogue, but in an SCP file… Maybe I should stick in some more interview logs.

item.title: SCP-TBD: The Extradimensional Grand Station: SCP-TBD: The Extradimensional Grand Station
item.content:encoded:
What if there was a subway system that went everywhere and everywhen? What if it went to pasts, presents, and futures where events unfolded differently? What wonderous possibilities could be waiting? And what untold horrors?

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up a lot of space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Document/Exploratory File

Elevator Pitch:

  • Entrance to anomaly first found in the form of an undocumented stairway in the New York City Subway shortly after 9/11.
  • This stairway, officially listed as SCP-TBD, also known as the Extradimensional Stairway by SCP personnel, leads to a massive series of passageways, officially listed as SCP-TBD-1
  • Visitors are guided by instances of artificial lifeforms consisting of programable matter/nanites. These instances take the form of the species they are interacting with.
  • This facility is controlled by a highly advanced AI system.
+ show block
– hide block
  • Due to the size of this facility, transportation to entrances are provided by a series of vacuum trains. According to readings provided by the onboard interfaces and the body-suit sensors worn by exploratory teams, these trains are capable of accelerating quickly to hypersonic speeds, but without producing the associated g-forces that would normally kill their occupants.

Central Narrative: Anomaly is a massive underground system that leads to an as yet undetermined number of places, including different planets and alternate realities. Various different species and alternate versions of humanity use this system, and the facility can be inhabited by a minimum of beings ranging in the thousands on any day.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The finished article will list exploratory expeditions to different planets in the prime reality, as well as into different timelines. Many different references to different SCPs and settings will be included, such as instances of SCP-682 being escorted back to their stairway entrance, one by an android dragging him in a stun net (kicking, screaming, and shouting insults and threats), while the witnessing MTF just looks on, and an instance of a reality where the Foundation and anomalies has been disclosed to the public.

Additional Notes:
This is my first SCP entry. I currently have two versions of this working in my head: one is more positive and optimistic, and is my preferred direction. Then there is another that is abandoned, inhabited by an insane AI, malfunctioning killer androids, and horrors from alternate dimensions that have wandered into the system. Idea is extrapolated from some dreams I've had in the past, namely the vast vacuum train system and stairways that go deep underground and into a maze of passageways.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: A new SCP I'm working on: Re: A new SCP I'm working on
item.content:encoded:
Ideas like this generally have the same flaw, that they seem like misery for the sake of misery. You've crafted a story about a kid getting tortured by the Foundation, but to what end? I'm not really getting a sense for a character arc or a real… narrative thread that's being followed and delivered upon.

I guess generally you should ask what the point of all this misery is. What sort of emotions are you attempting to evoke from your audience, and how do you plan to endear this main character to them?

item.title: A helping hand (Seeking Greenlight): A helping hand (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: This SCP involves a floating hand which assists people with things when they are needed, the SCP teleports to anyone who says they need help with something, this will not work if they are only thinking of needing help and not saying it,

Central Narrative: The hand is cut off at the wrist area, the inside shows a black void.
Testing showed that it can only help with things if it's within a 5 meter radius and will help with anything it can, it can hammer a nail in the wall, or shoot a target as long as it's within 5 meters of the person needing help.

It can't hold more than 15kg, it seems that anything put on the scp was taken with it, that's how the tracker was placed and kept tracking it, it seems to always help and has no sign of stopping but it only appears around 2 times per week max, and it will also do the task really fast, the foundation was able to snap one photo however

It is able to teleport anywhere on the world and wont stay any longer than needed so containment isn't possible and has since been classified as Euclid, it's presence was noticed by the foundation in 2011 when a twitter user Robert Hexain posted a message about the SCP who helped him repair his roof.

When there are multiple people in need of assistance it will randomly choose one to help and will help the other later if they still need help, during testing a tracker was put on the SCP to locate it at all times to see who the SCP helped, they will then be tracked down, interviewed and given Class B amnestics

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It can be helpful or it can be really dangerous

Additional Notes:

item.title: Seeking Greenlight - Man in the Mirror: Re: Seeking Greenlight - Man in the Mirror
item.content:encoded:
As a point of comparison, you may want to consider SCP-4052. It's not totally similar to your idea, in that the Foundation's rival is decidedly stronger to them in every way, but the point I want to draw is that the rival isn't just a Foundation clone. They're people with sandwich heads, and the reveal that their backronym is the same as the Foundation's is played as a joke at the end.

What's the PCS Foundation's history? If they're not anomalous, why are they and the Foundation so similar down to their backronyms? I'm not getting the sense that this is its own organization which rose to prominence in a similar way to the Foundation.
